concepts.name: Frictional Unemployment: Nature, Causes and Inevitability
key_dimensions: Definition and why it is considered 'voluntary' or transitional in nature
Role of information asymmetry and job-search costs in prolonging frictional unemployment
Why frictional unemployment persists even in a healthy, growing economy
Policy tools: job portals, employment exchanges, skill matching platforms — effectiveness vs. limitations

concepts.name: Structural Unemployment: Causes and Long-term Implications
key_dimensions: Distinction between structural unemployment caused by technological change vs. sectoral decline vs. geographic mismatch
Why structural unemployment is harder to address than frictional unemployment
India-specific drivers: automation in IT/BPO, agrarian distress leading to displaced rural labour
Structural unemployment vs. technological unemployment — overlap and distinction

concepts.name: Cyclical Unemployment: Business Cycle Linkage and Keynesian Framework
key_dimensions: Relationship between aggregate demand deficiency and cyclical unemployment (Keynesian explanation)
How cyclical unemployment differs from other types in its policy remedy — fiscal/monetary stimulus
COVID-19 pandemic as a case study of sudden cyclical unemployment spike in India
Okun's Law: relationship between GDP growth rate and unemployment rate change

concepts.name: Natural Rate of Unemployment (NRU) and Full Employment Equilibrium
key_dimensions: NRU = Frictional + Structural unemployment — why cyclical is excluded
NAIRU (Non-Accelerating Inflation Rate of Unemployment) — distinction from NRU and its policy significance
Why 'zero unemployment' is neither achievable nor desirable in a market economy
UPSC trap: confusing NRU with 'full employment' — full employment allows for NRU, not zero unemployment

concepts.name: Seasonal Unemployment: Definition, Indian Context and Policy Response
key_dimensions: How seasonal unemployment differs from cyclical unemployment — cyclical is macro-demand driven; seasonal is calendar/activity driven
Agriculture-dominant sectors in India — Kharif/Rabi cycles creating seasonal unemployment patterns
MGNREGS as a direct policy tool targeting seasonal unemployment in rural India
Overlap trap: seasonal unemployment can appear structural if seasonality is permanent and skills are non-transferable

concepts.name: Disguised Unemployment: Concept, Measurement and Indian Agriculture
key_dimensions: Definition: Marginal productivity of labour = zero; removal does not reduce output
Why disguised unemployment is invisible in standard unemployment statistics (Labour Force Survey)
Prevalence in Indian agriculture — surplus labour on family farms
Arthur Lewis Model: transfer of disguised unemployed to industrial sector as engine of growth

concepts.name: Underemployment vs. Unemployment: Conceptual Distinction and Measurement
key_dimensions: Underemployment: working below capacity (skill underutilization) vs. time-related underemployment (part-time involuntary)
ILO definition vs. India's PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey) measurement approach
Why underemployment is more relevant than open unemployment in India's informal economy context
UPSC trap: underemployment ≠ disguised unemployment — underemployed persons ARE working, disguised unemployed add no marginal output

concepts.name: Technological Unemployment: Automation, AI and Future of Work
key_dimensions: Relationship with structural unemployment — technological unemployment is a subset/cause of structural unemployment
Luddite Fallacy vs. real displacement concerns — historical debate and modern AI context
India's vulnerability: large low-skill workforce vs. automation in manufacturing and services
Policy responses: reskilling, social protection floors, universal basic income debate

concepts.name: Open Unemployment vs. Other Forms: Measurement Challenges in India
key_dimensions: Open unemployment: willing and able to work but finding no work — easiest to measure
Why open unemployment rate in India is low (~7-8%) despite widespread joblessness — disguised/underemployment absorbs surplus
Three measures in PLFS: Usual Status (US), Current Weekly Status (CWS), Current Daily Status (CDS)
CDS gives highest unemployment estimate — why UPSC often asks about which measure reveals true picture

concepts.name: Structural vs. Cyclical Unemployment: Policy Trap and Misdiagnosis Risk
key_dimensions: Why misidentifying structural unemployment as cyclical leads to policy failure (stimulus doesn't retrain workers)
Hysteresis effect: prolonged cyclical unemployment can become structural — skills atrophy, employability declines
India's post-COVID joblessness debate — structural (automation, formalization shock) vs. cyclical (demand collapse)
Supply-side vs. demand-side policy prescriptions as diagnostic test for the type of unemployment

concepts.name: Educated Unemployment: India-Specific Phenomenon
key_dimensions: Definition: unemployment among degree holders — higher open unemployment among graduates than illiterates in India
Causes: credential inflation, mismatch between university curriculum and industry needs, reservation for government jobs
Structural dimension: education system not aligned with labour market demand
National Education Policy 2020 and skill-based education reforms as policy response

concepts.name: Rural vs. Urban Unemployment Patterns in India
key_dimensions: Rural unemployment dominated by seasonal and disguised forms; urban by frictional and structural
PLFS data: urban unemployment rate consistently higher than rural — paradox explained by labour market formality
Reverse migration during COVID-19 — urban cyclical unemployment converting to rural disguised unemployment
MGNREGS (rural) vs. urban employment guarantee debate — recent policy discourse

concepts.name: Female Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) and Gender-Specific Unemployment
key_dimensions: India's female LFPR among lowest globally (~25%) — distinction between unemployment and labour force withdrawal
U-shaped relationship between income and female LFPR — withdrawal at middle-income, return at higher income
Structural barriers: social norms, care economy burden, safety concerns, wage discrimination
Recent PLFS data showing improvement — self-employment and agricultural work driving numbers, quality debate

concepts.name: Unemployment Rate Measurement: ILO Framework and India's PLFS
key_dimensions: ILO definition: unemployed = not working + available for work + actively seeking work — all three conditions must be met
UPSC trap: a discouraged worker who stops seeking work is NOT counted as unemployed — drops out of labour force
Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) vs. Worker Population Ratio (WPR) vs. Unemployment Rate — interrelationships
Why unemployment rate can fall even when employment conditions worsen (discouraged worker effect)

concepts.name: Jobless Growth Phenomenon: India's Growth-Employment Disconnect
key_dimensions: Definition: GDP growth without proportionate employment generation
India's experience post-2000: high GDP growth but declining WPR, especially in manufacturing
Capital-intensive growth, informalisation, and contractualisation as explanations
Structural implication: growth model needs reorientation toward labour-intensive sectors (textiles, leather, food processing)

concepts.name: Informalisation of Employment and Precarious Work
key_dimensions: Informal employment ≠ informal sector employment — formal sector firms also employ informal workers (contractual, casual)
Why informalisation blurs unemployment statistics — informal workers appear 'employed' but have zero job security
Gig economy workers: platform workers classified as self-employed, not captured in traditional unemployment data
Code on Social Security 2020 — attempt to extend coverage to gig/platform workers

concepts.name: Phillips Curve: Inflation-Unemployment Trade-off and Its Breakdown
key_dimensions: Original Phillips Curve: inverse relationship between unemployment and inflation — used for demand management
Stagflation of 1970s broke the Phillips Curve — simultaneous high inflation and high unemployment
Friedman-Phelps critique: only short-run trade-off exists; long-run Phillips Curve is vertical at NRU
India relevance: RBI's inflation targeting framework implicitly assumes some unemployment trade-off

concepts.name: Voluntary vs. Involuntary Unemployment: Classical vs. Keynesian Debate
key_dimensions: Classical view: all unemployment is voluntary — wages will adjust to clear labour market
Keynesian view: involuntary unemployment exists due to aggregate demand deficiency and wage rigidity
UPSC trap: frictional unemployment is often classified as 'voluntary'; cyclical is involuntary — but this is a simplification
Minimum wage laws, efficiency wages, and union bargaining as causes of involuntary unemployment above equilibrium

concepts.name: Employment Elasticity of Growth: Sectoral Variations and Policy Significance
key_dimensions: Employment elasticity = % change in employment / % change in output — measures job-creating capacity of growth
India data: agriculture has high elasticity but low productivity; services have low elasticity but high output share
Manufacturing employment elasticity declining — threat to 'Make in India' employment generation goal
Policy implication: targeting sectors with high elasticity AND decent wages (not just any employment) — quality vs. quantity

concepts.name: MGNREGS as Counter-Cyclical Employment Policy: Design, Achievements and Criticisms
key_dimensions: Legal guarantee of 100 days employment — demand-driven, not supply-driven (UPSC frequently tests this distinction)
Counter-cyclical design: automatically expands during recessions/droughts without legislative action
Criticisms: wage below market rate in many states, asset quality concerns, administrative leakages
MGNREGS primarily addresses seasonal/disguised unemployment in rural areas — does NOT address structural unemployment
